message.content:
Mitochondria are found in almost all eukaryotic cells.  
The number of mitochondria per cell varies widely depending on the cell’s type and energy demands:

| Cell type | Typical number of mitochondria per cell |
|-----------|----------------------------------------|
| Most mammalian somatic cells | ~100–200 |
| Muscle cells (especially cardiac) | Several hundred to a few thousand |
| Neurons (high‑energy demand) | Hundreds to thousands |
| Sperm cells | Thousands (to power motility) |

So while a “typical” cell may contain on the order of a few hundred mitochondria, specialized cells can have far more or fewer.
